_about: The narrative map: the claims the discourse is making about the world, each as a hypothesis with a sign, the words that identify it in a gathered item (matched deterministically, case-insensitive, substring), the measurable predictions it implies (a registered fork, a history-layer outcome, a field condition), the observation that would falsify it, and the incentive tags a reader may discount by. Entries are added when the sweeps show a claim held by two independent holders or one holder plus a data anomaly; they are never removed, only retired with the date. Statements paraphrase the holders; the verbatim positions stay in the ledger beside them.

narratives.title: The AI buildout is a debt-financed capex bubble that breaks when the money runs out
narratives.statement: As held: capex has run past cash flow and is increasingly debt-funded; the chain below the principals (neoclouds, labs, suppliers) defects first — deferrals, cancellations, shelved deals, rental prices — and the bust arrives through credit transmission rather than through anyone's guidance.

narratives.title: China holds hidden foreign-exchange assets that underpin a weak renminbi and its export outperformance
narratives.statement: As held: FX settlement purchases of $500-600bn a year against a flat PBOC balance sheet, missing reinvested interest and entrusted loans to the policy banks add up to a trillion-dollar gap; the pattern looks like backdoor intervention around a crawling peg.
narratives.falsifier: A PBOC disclosure reconciling the gap, or the renminbi floating outside the band without intervention.

_matching: A keyword must start at a word boundary and may be the stem of a longer word ('refinanc' finds 'refinancing'); matching is case-insensitive on name, title, position, sign_basis and the number claims of each voices item. A match needs one strong word or two weak ones. Holders are matched items whose sign agrees with the narrative's; opposed items are matched items of the opposite sign that hit a strong word.
